metadata.keywords: typography, punctuation, french, canadian french, fr-CA, no-break space

blocks.text: Two French conventions exist. European French ("fr", sample 03) puts a narrow no-break space before ? ! ; and a no-break space before : and inside « ». Canadian French ("fr-CA", OQLF) keeps the no-break space before the colon and inside the guillemets, and sets ? ! ; against the word. The two presets must produce different files: in pdfnative 1.7 they did not, because both no-break spaces were folded to a plain space before reaching the font — 1.8.0 draws the font's own U+00A0 and U+202F.

pdfnative extract-text returns the characters the file carries: under fr-CA the colon is preceded by U+00A0 and the question mark by nothing; under fr it is preceded by U+202F. Both need a registered font (--font latin --lang latin): the base-14 fonts have no such glyphs and fall back to a plain space.
